item.text: The model is a small linear program: represent each residual as positive minus negative parts, then minimize the weighted sum of those parts. This directly encodes the check loss and avoids unavailable regression packages.

The first implementation exposed a scalability issue in the generic formulation: building dense residual-identity matrices is unnecessarily large for this dataset. I’m switching those matrices to sparse form, which preserves the exact linear program while keeping memory bounded.

item.text: All visible tests pass, but the direct residual LP takes about a minute because it carries one pair of auxiliary variables per row. I’m tightening the formulation by grouping identical covariate patterns and representing each group’s check-loss curve with its exact piecewise-linear supporting lines; this keeps the same mathematical objective but is much faster.

The optimized implementation now passes all six tests, and the command-line output matches the expected median and 90th-percentile effects (including the larger top-decile incarceration penalty). I’m doing one final review of the diff and test status.
